summary: The seat comes to you: Fewer people filed than there were seats, and enough voters wrote you in that {clerk} has to ask whether you will take {open seat}.
realLife: One life: In 2022 in Boonsboro, Maryland, two candidates filed for three council seats. Counting ballots on the election board, he kept hearing his own name, won the third seat on write-ins, and accepted it. Another: He missed the ballot deadline in Winooski, Vermont, and won a council seat as a write-in with stickers, posters and postcards.
gates: Fewer candidates filed than seats were open.

branches.then: You hear your own name read again and again, and the other counters look at you before {clerk} says a word.
{household member} reminds you that you swore off this kind of thing, or tells you to take it.
